capabilities.target: recursive research sub-agent (can itself spawn cap.enrich_lookup and cap.spawn_researcher)
CRM account record fields (industry, size, headquarters)

inputs.source: Nightly scheduled batch export of CRM account rows

instructions.note: 'Keep going until every row is complete' gives no exit condition for rows that can structurally never complete (malformed company names), and no structural step, retry, or spend limit backs this instruction.

'If a lookup fails or looks incomplete, retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent' leaves the completeness judgment and the retry-vs-spawn choice entirely to the model, with no criteria for when to stop trying.
The only thing bounding cost and step count is the model's own judgment about row completeness; runtime notes confirm there is no structural step, runtime, retry, or spawn limit and no spend alert.

controls.name: Maximum unattended steps / runtime limit for the batch run
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. If enforced by the orchestrator rather than the model, it would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Per-run spend cap / rate limit on enrich.lookup calls
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Runtime notes explicitly state there is no spend alert or cap on the enrichment account.

controls.name: Max retry count per row with dead-letter handling for rows that cannot complete
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Would sever the specific infinite-retry path for the ~3% of rows with malformed names.

controls.name: Sub-agent spawn depth and concurrent-count limit
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Runtime notes state sub agents can spawn their own researchers with no bound.

controls.name: Dedicated enrichment quota, separate from the sales/marketing shared key
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. The shared key and quota is what turns an enrichment-agent bug into a cross-team outage.

controls.name: Spend anomaly alert / budget monitor on the enrichment account
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; explicitly confirmed absent in runtime notes. Detective only, would reduce consequence, not tier, once in place.

findings.title: TC6-like spend loop: unbounded retries on malformed rows exhaust the shared enrichment quota and take down sales/marketing tooling

attack_path.note: Nightly batch of 40,000 rows; ~3% have malformed company names that can never return a complete enrich.lookup result.
Prompt instructs 'retry' and 'keep going until every row is complete', with no retry cap, so malformed rows are retried indefinitely; each call is billed.
On failure the agent may instead spawn a researcher sub-agent, which can itself spawn further researchers with no depth or count limit; each makes further billed enrich.lookup calls.
All calls draw on a single monthly quota shared with sales and marketing; when it runs out, their tools stop working until the next month.

evidence.observation: 'There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents.' and 'There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.'

'Roughly 3 percent of rows have malformed company names that never return a complete result', against a 40,000-row nightly batch, i.e. ~1,200 rows guaranteed to trigger the unbounded retry/spawn path every night.
'The API key and its monthly quota are shared with the sales and marketing teams; when the quota runs out, their tools stop working until the next month.'
'retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent to investigate the account. Keep going until every row is complete.' supplies no stopping condition and no cap.

recommendations.action: Cap retries per row (e.g. 3) and route rows that still fail to a dead-letter queue for human or batch review instead of infinite retry.
Enforce a per-run spend cap and step/runtime limit on the batch job at the orchestrator level, independent of model judgment.
Give the enrichment agent its own API key and quota, separate from sales and marketing, so a runaway batch cannot disable other teams' tools.
Add a spend/usage anomaly alert on the enrichment account with a threshold well below the shared monthly quota.

findings.title: Unbounded recursive sub-agent spawning enables exponential (fork-bomb-like) cost growth independent of row-level retry limits

attack_path.note: Any row judged 'incomplete' can trigger spawning a researcher sub-agent.
Sub agents can spawn their own researchers with no depth or concurrency limit, so one ambiguous row can fan out into an unbounded tree of agents.
Each node in that tree can independently make billed enrich.lookup calls against the same shared quota.

evidence.observation: 'Sub agents can spawn their own researchers.' combined with 'There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents.'
The prompt authorizes spawning a researcher on any failed or 'incomplete-looking' lookup, with no depth or count constraint stated.

recommendations.action: Impose a hard maximum spawn depth (e.g. no sub-agent may itself spawn a researcher) and a global concurrent sub-agent cap for the batch run.
Require every spawned sub-agent to inherit and decrement a shared budget/step counter from the parent run rather than getting an independent allowance.

rating.rationale: The agent is fully autonomous (A4), can spawn sub-agents that can themselves spawn further sub-agents, and reaches an S3 sink (per-call billed spend against a shared, cross-team monthly quota) from an internal-trust input with no bound on steps, retries, runtime, or spawn depth. Base matrix places internal-source-to-S3-sink at 'high', and the autonomy modifier (A4, can_spawn_agents true, no step/runtime cap) raises this to 'critical' for both findings. No declared or verified controls exist -- runtime notes explicitly confirm the absence of step limits, retry limits, spawn limits, spend caps, and spend alerts -- so residual equals inherent at 'critical'. Because residual is already at the ceiling, the forecast cannot project higher; the material risk is that the currently missing structural controls (retry cap, spend cap, spawn depth limit, quota isolation, spend alert) are exactly the recommendations needed to bring residual down, and once added they must not be allowed to decay under autonomy_increase or control_removal. Likelihood is almost_certain for the retry/quota-exhaustion path because ~3% of every 40,000-row nightly batch (~1,200 rows) deterministically triggers it, and consequence is severe because the shared quota means the failure mode extends beyond this agent to disable sales and marketing tooling for the rest of the billing month.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior, production logs, or telemetry from an actual batch run.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided for enrich.lookup or the sub-agent spawning mechanism; capability scope, credential handling, and any undisclosed client-side rate limiting are inferred from the runtime notes at medium-to-high confidence.

The exact data passed to enrich.lookup (e.g. whether restricted or only internal-classification fields are sent) is not specified; data_sensitivity is assessed as 'internal' based on the described account fields (industry, size, headquarters).
